articles.name: How to add an SRV record
articles.title: How to add an SRV record
articles.body:
An SRV record is a record used to identify the server using a hostname and port number for services such as VOIP.

Adding an SRV record

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click on the site where you want to add the SRV record
  3. Navigate to Domains
  4. Click on Manage DNS for the website where you want to add the SRV record
  5. Find and click the Add a DNS record button

    A dropdown menu will appear.

  6. Under Type, choose SRV

    Important:

    You will need to provide the specific details for your SRV record, the Priority number, the Port number, the Weight number. If you do not have this information, you will need to ask the service provider for the information in order to add the record.

  7. Add Priority, Port, and Weight values in their corresponding fields
  8. In the Hostname field, add your service(type of service) and protocol (transport protocol) values in this format:  _service._protocol

    For example, _sip._tls

  9. In the second Hostname field, input your target value. For example, address.yourdomain.com
  10. Click the Add DNS Record button to complete the process and add your new SRV record

articles.name: How to Increase PHP Config Limitations
articles.title: How to Increase PHP Config Limitations
articles.body:
PHP configuration limitations can vary depending on the hosting environment, the PHP version, and any additional restrictions imposed by system administrators.

Default limitations for PHP configurations

  • memory_limit = 256M (Memory limit)
  • post_max_size = 128M (Post Max Size)
  • max_execution_time = 300 (Max execution time)
  • max_input_time = 300 (Max input time)
  • upload_max_filesize = 128M (Upload max filesize)
  • opcache.save_comments = turned off by default
  • pm.max_children = 3 (PHP workers)

If the default limitations are causing issues with your website, you can increase the limitations from your 10Web dashboard. 

Important:

If you want to increase your PHP workers or the limitation pm.max_children, you will need to contact customer support via live chat. Please note that the highest value we can set for PHP workers is 5.

How to change your PHP config limitations

To change the limitations of your PHP configuration:

  1. Log in to your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click on the website where you want to make the change
  3. Click on Hosting Services > Tools
  4. Navigate to the bottom of the page and click on Advanced settings
  5. To change the limit, click on the drop-down arrow next to the configuration and choose to double or triple the limit
  6. Click Save to apply the new limitation

articles.name: Troubleshooting a Blocked REST Route
articles.title: Troubleshooting a Blocked REST Route
articles.body:
REST stands for Representational State Transfer, and it's a set of principles that define how web standards, like HTTP and URI, should be used. A REST route refers to a specific URL pattern in a web application that is handled by a particular function or method. These routes are the endpoints of a RESTful API and correspond to specific operations based on the HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.) used. 

Reasons why REST route may be blocked

Firewall or Security Groups

Sometimes security measures may block incoming requests to certain IP addresses or ports. If the server running the REST API is behind a firewall or inside a network with strict security rules, certain requests might not reach the server.

CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) Policy

This is a security measure implemented in web browsers to prevent requests from being made between different domains, unless explicitly allowed by the server. If a REST route is being accessed from a different domain, and the server does not allow it, then the request will be blocked.

Rate Limiting

To protect the server from being overwhelmed by too many requests, some APIs implement rate limiting. If too many requests are sent in a certain period of time, subsequent requests may be blocked.

Authentication/Authorization

If the route requires certain authentication or authorization and the request does not meet these criteria, the request will be denied.

IP Blocking

The server may be set to block requests from certain IP addresses, usually as a security measure.

How to check if the REST route is blocked

To check if the REST route is blocked, navigate to Get URL with Curl and check these two links:

You can directly access the the get curl website for checking if REST is blocked by using this link: https://reqbin.com/req/c-1n4ljxb9/curl-get-request-example.

curl https://yourdomain.com/?rest_route=/tenweb/v1/get_check 
curl -X POST https://yourdomain.com/?rest_route=/tenweb/v1/post_check, 

replacing yourdomain.com with your website URL. 

If you receive {“code”:“ok”}, then the route is functioning. If you get anything different (like rest no route), you will need to fix your REST route.  

How to fix a blocked REST route

If you check your REST route and get anything other than “code”:”ok” you can try fixing the REST route by:

  1. Deactivating any security plugin/service that might affect the API or REST

    Next check if your REST route is blocked using the above instructions.

    If this doesn’t work, then: 

  2. Contact your hosting service provider and ask them to whitelist our IP addresses listed below.

10Web IP address:

articles.name: Troubleshooting 10Web Subdomain References After Pointing Custom Domain Name
articles.title: Troubleshooting 10Web Subdomain References After Pointing Custom Domain Name
articles.body:
Your website is assigned a 10Web subdomain when first created. For example, the website’s address may end with .10web.site or .10web.cloud. However, you can point your own domain name from another registrar or you can get a custom domain name directly from 10Web. 

Once you point your domain and set it as the primary, the 10Web subdomain is automatically replaced. If you still encounter the 10Web subdomain in any areas of your live website, please follow the below instructions.

Primary domain redirecting to 10Web subdomain 

If you have already pointed your domain to 10Web and made it the primary one, but it still redirects to a .10web subdomain, try the following steps:

Step 1: Make domain primary again

  1. From your 10Web Dashboard, click Manage on the website experiencing issues.
  2. Go to the Domains section.
  3. Click Make Primary next to the 10Web subdomain to make it primary again.
  4. Click Confirm.
  5. Click Make Primary next to your domain name again to make it the primary domain.
  6. Click Confirm. 

Step 2: Clear website cache

  1. Click Manage on the website experiencing issues
  2. Locate Hosting Services > Tools section. 
  3. Click Clear Cache. 

Note:

If you are using Cloudflare Enterprise CDN provided by 10Web, clear its cache from the Website Booster > Cloudflare CDN section as well. 

Step 2: Change the URL directly from database

If the issue persists after completing the above steps, please proceed with changes directly from the database.

  1. Connect to your website database from the Hosting Services > Credentials section of your 10Web Dashboard. Here is how. 
  2. In the database manager, find and select the live_database associated with your site.
  3. In phpMyAdmin, double-click the wp-options table to open it.
  4. Find the siteurl and home entries within the wp-options table, and click Edit next to each one. 

    Note:

    Your website link should follow this format: https://yourdomain.com.

  5. Enter the correct WordPress site URL in the option_value field for both entries.
  6. Click Go to save your changes.
  7. Clear your website cache again as described in Step 2. 
  8. Reload your website to make sure it's functioning as expected.

10Web subdomain visible in your sitemap or via inspect element

If 10Web subdomain still appears in areas such as the inspect element or sitemap after setting up your custom domain name, follow the steps below. 

Step 1: Regenerate files and data with Elementor

  1. Log into your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Navigate to Elementor on the left menu of your WordPress dashboard.
  3. From the drop-down list select Tools.
  4. Locate and click on the Regenerate Files and Data button.
  5. Click Save Changes.
  6. Hover on  Manage 10Web Cache button from the dashboard header.
  7. Click on the Clear all cache button.

In case you are still facing issues, follow the step below. 

Step 2: Replace your domain name using a plugin

Note:

If you are using Elementor for your website, you can replace your domain name from WordPress Dashboard > Elementor > Tools > Replace URL section. 

  1. Log into your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Navigate to the Plugins section and click on Add New.
  3. Search for the Better Search Replace plugin.
  4. Install and activate the plugin.
  5. Open the Better Search Replace plugin from the Tools section of WordPress dashboard.
  6. In the Search for field, enter your 10Web subdomain.
  7. In the Replace with field, enter your new domain name.

    Note:

    The links should follow this format: https://yourdomain.com.

  8. Select the data tables you want to modify, ensuring that those created by your SEO plugin are included.
  9. Uncheck the Run as dry run option.
  10. Click Run Search/Replace to complete the process.
  11. Hover on  Manage 10Web Cache button from the dashboard header.
  12. Click on the Clear all cache button.

Conclusion

While pointing a custom domain to your 10Web website typically replaces the default 10Web subdomain, you may encounter scenarios where the subdomain still appears. By thoroughly following these procedures, you can ensure that your custom domain is properly reflected across your site, eliminating any remaining references to the 10Web subdomain.

articles.name: How to Import an SQL File into the Database
articles.title: How to Import an SQL File into the Database
articles.body:
Sometimes, you need to import an SQL file into your website's database. This could be due to a number of reasons like migration, backup, or testing. Here at 10Web, we provide two methods for importing an SQL file: via phpMyAdmin and via SSH and SFTP. We'll guide you through both methods.

Importing via phpMyAdmin

Note:

The SQL file should have the proper format.

We recommend trying this method first, as it's user-friendly and accessible right from your 10Web dashboard. 

Here are the steps:

  1. Go to the 10web dashboard
  2. Click Manage on the website you want to import the database to
  3. Click on Credentials under the Hosting Services in the left menu
  4. Click on Open MySQL in the Database Access section
  5. Copy and paste the username and password found on the Credentials page and click Log in
  6. Select the database from the left menu in phpMyAdmin
  7. Click the Import tab
  8. Click Choose File under the Files to Import section
  9. Click Go in the bottom right corner to begin the import

If you experience an error using this method, it may be due to the SQL file’s size. In that case, please try to import the file using SSH and SFTP.

Importing via SSH and SFTP

This method is a bit more technical, but it will handle larger SQL files effectively.

Before you start, ensure you have your SQL file ready and access to SFTP and SSH for your website.

Step 1: Upload your SQL file

The first step is to upload your SQL file to your website using SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol). 

To accomplish this:

  1. Open your SFTP client software (for example, FileZilla)
  2. Connect to your website's server using your SFTP credentials
  3. Navigate to the /home/wplive/web/wp-live/ folder in your website's file directory
  4. Upload your SQL file (e.g., `example.sql`) into the wp-live folder

After this, your SQL file path will be /home/wplive/web/wp-live/example.sql.

Step 2: Import the SQL file via SSH

After uploading your SQL file, the next step is to import it into the database using SSH (Secure Shell). 

Here's how to do it:

  1. Connect to your website's server using SSH.
  2. Run the following command: mysql -u MYSQL_USERNAME -h mysql.10web.site --binary-mode MYSQL_DB_NAME < /home/wplive/web/wp-live/example.sql

Important:

Please note that in the above command, you'll need to replace MYSQL_USERNAME and MYSQL_DB_NAME with the appropriate values from your wp-config.php file. Remember to change example.sql to your SQL file’s name.

Role of Website Blockers 

Certain websites incorporate security measures, often called blockers, to protect their content from being accessed by automated tools or web crawlers. These blockers view the automated attempts by the AI Builder as potential threats, thereby preventing access and resulting in the This site can't be reached error.

Impact on AI Recreation 

Because of these blockers, the AI Recreation feature might not be able to access and recreate certain websites. Essentially, the feature works by accessing websites, reading their structure, and then recreating that structure. But, if a website has a blocker that prevents access, AI Recreation won't be able to function as intended for that specific site.

Ongoing Improvements 

We understand that this limitation can be frustrating for our users, and we want you to know that we're working on it. Our team at 10Web is continuously improving our AI technology, finding ways to negotiate with these blockers without violating the website's security or integrity.

articles.name: Troubleshooting 429 Too Many Requests Error
articles.title: Troubleshooting 429 Too Many Requests Error
articles.body:
The 429 "Too Many Requests" error means a user or system has exceeded the allowed number of requests in a given timeframe. It helps prevent DoS attacks and ensures server and API reliability.

Causes of "429 Too Many Requests" error

For website users, a 429 error usually means too many requests or actions were made in a short time. This can occur due to:

  • Rapidly refreshing a webpage: Continuously reloading a webpage within a short time frame can trigger the rate limit, resulting in a 429 error.
  • Submitting multiple form requests: Quickly filling out and submitting multiple forms can lead to exceeding the allowed number of requests.
  • High-frequency resource access: Frequently accessing or requesting resources from the server in a short period can breach the rate limits.
  • Automated scripts and bots: Web crawlers, data scrapers, or other automated scripts that perform bulk operations or fetch large amounts of data rapidly can also trigger a 429 error. These tools often send a high number of requests within a short period, leading to rate limit breaches.

Bots and Automated Scripts, such as web crawlers, data scrapers, or other bots, can also trigger a 429 error if they exceed the allowed number of API requests within a short timeframe. This is especially relevant for scripts that perform bulk operations or fetch large amounts of data rapidly.

Important:

If you encounter the 429 Too Many Requests error when using crawling tools like Screaming Frog or SEMrush, contact 10Web support team and we will change the Rate Limitation for the required tool.

Fixing "429 Too Many Requests" error

Step 1: Wait and retry

The first step in resolving the HTTP 429 error is to acknowledge that it often occurs due to sending too many requests in a short time. In such cases, the simplest solution is to wait for some time and then attempt the request again. This temporary pause allows the system to reset, and often, retrying the action after waiting will resolve the issue without further intervention. 

Step 2: Check for WordPress plugin and theme conflicts

To check if a specific plugin or theme is causing the problem, you can temporarily deactivate them.

Case 1: If you have access to WordPress dashboard

  1. Head to the Plugins section of your WordPress dashboard. 
  2. Choose all your plugins using the checkmark. 
  3. Choose Deactivate from the dropdown menu of Bulk Actions. 
  4. Click Apply. 
  5. If the issue is solved, enable your plugins back one by one to find the exact plugin causing the issue.

Case 2: If you don’t have access to WordPress dashboard

  1. Use SFTP to connect to your website files.
  2. Double click on the web > wp-live folder to locate the plugins folder.
  3. Right-click on the folder and rename it.  
  4. Try to access your website. If the error is resolved, it indicates that one or more of your active plugins are either corrupted or outdated. 
  5. Rename the folder back to plugins and troubleshoot each plugin individually by checking their folders.

Step 3: Restore backup

If you are still facing the issue, restoring your website from a previous backup might be the solution. 10Web offers automated backups that can be restored through your 10Web dashboard. To restore a backup: 

  1. Go to 10Web dashboard menu and navigate to the Backups section.
  2. Select the backup you wish to restore from the list.
  3. Navigate to the Restore button.
  4. Confirm the restoration in the same environment it was created. 

Note:

Always ensure you’re restoring from a recent backup to avoid losing valuable data.

Step 4: Contact customer care

If the previous steps didn’t resolve the issue, you can contact customer care via our 24/7 live chat. Our team is available around the clock to assist you with persistent HTTP 429 errors. We can review your usage patterns and, if necessary, adjust your rate limit to better suit your needs, ensuring your activities are supported without disruption.

Conclusion

The HTTP 429 error is a client-side issue triggered when the server receives an overwhelming number of requests. If not addressed promptly, this error can hinder the functionality of third-party APIs and block search engines from properly crawling your website. Therefore, it’s essential to resolve the "429 Too Many Requests" error swiftly to maintain optimal website performance and functionality.

articles.name: Resolving "DNS Zone Limit Exceeded Error" Message

articles.body:
A DNS zone contains the DNS records for your domain, such as its IP address and other settings. When you exceed the allowed number of zones, "DNS Zone Limit Exceeded" error is triggered. Encountering this error can be frustrating, especially when you can't access the Manage DNS button in your dashboard. This error typically occurs when the number of DNS zones, which corresponds to the number of your websites plus one, has been surpassed.

Fixing DNS Zone Limit Exceeded error

Step 1: Delete unused DNS zones

  1. Go to your 10Web Dashboard.
  2. Click on Manage and open the Domains section.
  3. Look for any domains or DNS zones that you no longer need.
  4. Click on 3 dots and remove these unused zones to free up space for new domains.

Step 2: Point your domain using an A-record from another DNS provider

If you don’t want to delete any zones or need more than your current limit allows, you can use a different DNS provider. To do this, set up an A-record in the other provider’s DNS settings to point your domain to your desired IP address.

By either deleting unused zones or pointing your domain to an external DNS, you can easily resolve the "DNS Zone Limit Exceeded" error and manage your domains again.

articles.name: How to Locate and Exclude JS Files in the 10Web Website Booster
articles.title: How to Locate and Exclude JS Files in the 10Web Website Booster
articles.body:
10Web Website Booster plugin enhances your website's performance. However, occasionally it may conflict with certain JavaScript (JS) files on your website, leading to functionality issues. 

Important:

This guide is for more advanced users who are familiar with working with JavaScript. If you are not familiar or are a beginner, we recommend using the One click exclusion feature in the advanced settings of 10Web Booster.

This guide will navigate you through three different scenarios:

  • When there are Uncaught TypeErrors in the console
  • When there are no errors, but the plugin or theme is not functioning correctly
  • When there's an issue with a third-party service's JS

Important:

Before starting with any scenario, you need to open both optimized and non-optimized versions of your website.

How to open the non-optimized version of your website

  1. Launch your website in Google Chrome
  2. Add ?two_nooptimize=1 to the end of your website's URL to open the non-optimized version of your webpage

For example, change www.example.com to www.example.com?two_nooptimize=1, then press Enter.

Dealing with uncaught TypeErrors in the console

Identify error messages

  1. Right-click anywhere on your optimized webpage and select Inspect
  2. Navigate to the Console tab

    Error messages related to problematic JS files will display. 

  3. Specifically, look for Uncaught TypeError: XYZ is not a function or or Uncaught ReferenceError: XYZ is not defined

These errors indicate an issue with a specific JS function or variable.

Exclude the problematic function

  1. Go to 10Web dashboard > Website Booster > Settings
  2. In the Excluded JavaScript File field, enter the function name, in this case XYZ, causing the error
  3. Save your changes

If the Uncaught TypeError of the optimized version has changed with another uncaught type error, you should exclude that new function as well. If the same Uncaught TypeError persists after excluding the function, you will need to identify the JS file that contains this function and exclude it. 

Here's how:

  1. Copy the function name from the error message
  2. Open the non-optimized version of your webpage
  3. Right-click anywhere on your non-optimized webpage and select Inspect
  4. Navigate to the Sources tab   
  5. Click CTRL+SHIFT+F on Windows (CMD+OPTION+F on Mac) and paste the function name into the search field

    This way, you'll see in which JS files the function is called

  6. Copy the js file names where the function is called i.e.  example.js
  7. Paste them into the Excluded JavaScript File field of the 10Web Booster Settings
  8. Save your changes

Specific errors and exclusions

  • If you encounter Uncaught TypeError: e.indexOf is not a function or Uncaught ReferenceError: wp is not defined, you should exclude wp-includes/ in the  Exclude JavaScript File field.
  • If you encounter an Uncaught ReferenceError: jQuery is not defined error message, exclude jquery.min.js.

Plugin or theme is not functioning properly

If there are no errors in the console, but your theme or plugin is not working as expected, or the issue has not resolved by simply excluding some js files:

  1. Navigate to Website Booster > Settings > One-click exclusions
  2. Identify and select the checkbox next to the problematic plugin/theme to exclude it from optimization
  3. Save your changes

Important:

Often the issue can be caused by the builder plugin/theme your website uses. If the issue persists, you should exclude the builder plugin/theme as well.

Problem with third-party service JS

If a third-party service is not functioning correctly on your website:

  1. Navigate to the non-optimized page where the third-party service should function
  2. Right-click and select Inspect
  3. Navigate to the Network tab
  4. In the Filter bar, click on .js to display only JavaScript files
  5. Reload your webpage
  6. In the Name column, look for .js files related to the third-party service

Quick tip:

The name or URL of these files often includes the service's name. For example, for a service called ThirdPartyService, you might see a file named thirdpartyservice.js. Please be aware that the JavaScript file name may be abbreviated or presented in the form of a slug.  You can hover over the JS file to view the complete name.

Once identified:

  1. Go to 10Web dashboard > Website Booster > Settings
  2. In the Excluded JavaScript File field, enter the js file name, in this case thirdpartyservice.js, causing the error

    Important:

    If there are multiple JS files loading from the same external source, we recommend that you exclude all its files using its main URL. For example, if the URL of all external JS files of the third party service begin with https://externalsource.com/, this is its main URL and this is what you should exclude.

  3. Save your changes

By following these steps, you can exclude any problematic JS files or functions, ensuring your website runs smoothly.

Note:

Every website is unique and may have different JS files or functions that need to be excluded. If you're still facing issues after following these steps, try a lower level of optimization.

articles.name: How to Locate and Exclude CSS Files in the 10Web Website Booster

articles.body:
10Web Speed Booster is a powerful WordPress plugin that improves website load times by optimizing elements like CSS files. While effective, these optimizations can sometimes affect your site's design or functionality. This guide shows you how to identify and exclude problematic CSS files using the Excluded CSS Files feature.

Important:

This guide is for more advanced users who are familiar with working with CSS. If you are not familiar or are a beginner, we recommend disabling the critical CSS feature in the advanced settings of 10Web Booster.

Locating the problematic CSS files

The first step in troubleshooting is to identify the CSS files causing the issues. This process can be carried out using your browser's built-in inspection tools. We'll use Google Chrome as an example for the instructions below:

Access the non-optimized version of your website

  1. Open your website in Google Chrome.
  2. Add ?two_nooptimize=1 to the end of your website's URL to view the non-optimized version of your website

    For example, if your website is www.example.com, you would enter www.example.com?two_nooptimize=1

  3. Press enter to load the non-optimized version of your website

Use the select an element in the page to inspect it tool

  1. Right-click anywhere on the non-optimized version of your website and select Inspect from the dropdown menu.

    This will open the Developer Tools panel on the right-hand side or at the bottom of your browser.

    At the top left corner of the Developer Tools panel, you'll see an icon that looks like a square with a cursor. This is the Select an element in the page to inspect it tool. 

  2. Click on this icon

    Once the tool is active, you can move your cursor around your website. Different sections of your website will be highlighted as you hover over them. 

  3. Navigate to the element that isn't displaying correctly.

    For example, a button on your page is not styled correctly. 

  4. Hover over that button and click on it.

Identifying the CSS file

The HTML code for the element you clicked and the CSS rules that style it will appear in the panel. Each CSS rule comes with a file name and a line number, such as style.css:30. 

  1. Right-click on it and select Open in new tab

    This will open the CSS file associated with the problematic element. In the new tab, you'll see the URL of the CSS file. 

  2. Copy the URL starting from /plugins/ or /themes/

    For example, if the URL is www.example.com/wp-content/plugins/my-plugin/style.css, you would copy /plugins/my-plugin/style.css.

  3. Follow the steps in the Excluding CSS files section to exclude the files

Note:

If you can't find the exact CSS file, it's possible to exclude the entire plugin or theme folder by excluding the /plugin/my-plugin folder or /plugin/my-theme folder.

Locating the problematic CSS files for Safari users

Enable the develop menu

  1. Open Safari 
  2. Click on Safari in the menu bar at the top, then select Preferences
  3. In the Preferences window, select the Advanced tab.
  4. Check the box that says Show Develop menu in menu bar

Open the Non-Optimized Version of Your Website

  1. Open your website in Safari
  2. Append ?two_nooptimize=1 to the end of your website's URL in the address bar, then press Enter.

Inspect your website

Control-click (or right-click) an element that's not displaying correctly, then select Inspect Element. The web inspector will open, showing the HTML and CSS for your site.

Identify the CSS file

On the right side of the web inspector, you'll see the CSS rules that apply to the selected element. Each CSS rule has a file name and a line number, such as style.css:30. 

  1. Control-click (or right-click) on it and select Open in new tab

    This will open the CSS file associated with the problematic element. In the new tab, you'll see the URL of the CSS file. 

  2. Copy the URL, starting from /plugins/ or /themes/

    For example, if the URL is www.example.com/wp-content/plugins/my-plugin/style.css, you would copy /plugins/my-plugin/style.css.

  3. Follow the steps in the Excluding CSS files section to exclude the files

Excluding CSS files

After identifying a problematic CSS file, you can exclude it from 10Web Booster's optimization process.

  1. Log in to your 10Web dashboard.
  2. Click on the site where you're facing the issue
  3. Navigate to Website Booster > Settings
  4. Scroll down to the Advanced Settings section
  5. Paste the copied URL into the Excluded CSS Files field in the 10Web dashboard.
  6. Click Save 

The specified CSS file is now excluded from the optimization process, and any issues it was causing should be resolved.

articles.name: How to Troubleshoot and Resolve Issues Caused by 10Web Booster
articles.title: How to Troubleshoot and Resolve Issues Caused by 10Web Booster
articles.body:
10Web Booster is a potent tool that utilizes over 35 optimization techniques such as JS delay, critical CSS, Lazy Load, and more, to improve your website's performance. Depending on the combination of plugins/themes used by your website, the tool may potentially cause issues. Let's look at how to troubleshoot and resolve some common challenges.

Important:

Any time you make changes to your Website Booster settings, remember to clear your caches so you can see the changes. Click the Clear Cache button found in the 10Web Dashboard > Website Booster > Settings. You may also need to clear your browser cache or try checking the changes in a new incognito window.

Fixing issues with images

Issues with images can often be traced back to the Lazy Load feature of the 10Web Booster. Problems you might encounter include:

  • Missing images 
  • Disappeared background images
  • Incomplete loading images

To resolve these issues:

  1. Navigate to the Website Booster > Settings in your 10Web dashboard
  2. If you’re having issues with images, locate the Lazy Load for images 
  3. If you’re having issues with background images, locate the Lazy Load for background images
  4. Disable these options by ticking the checkmark off
  5. Click Save to apply the changes
  6. Click Clear Cache

To check if images are now working, try visiting the page experiencing image issues in an incognito window. 

Fixing issues with fonts

Font issues can present as:

  • Unwanted changes in font size and style
  • Icons appearing as squares or going missing
  • Unexpected font substitutions
  • Distorted or overlapping text

To rectify these problems:

  1. Navigate to the Website Booster > Settings in your 10Web dashboard
  2. Go to Font optimizer and click on the drop-down menu
  3. Select each optimization level to determine which one fixes the issue
  4. Click Save to implement the changes
  5. If the two levels do not fix the issue, choose No optimization 

If the problem persists, you can exclude the CSS file responsible for your fonts from being optimized. 

Fixing issues with plugins/themes/services

Some issues with plugins/themes might manifest as:

  • Missing sections of a plugin or theme
  • Plugin or theme malfunctioning
  • Incorrect rendering of plugin/theme elements
  • Unexpected layout changes
  • Slider malfunctioning/missing slider
  • Malfunctioning of third-party analytics, SEO, marketing and advertising tools, customer support systems, etc. 
  • Malfunctioning/missing other JS libraries

To address these issues:

  1. Go to the Website Booster > Settings in your 10Web dashboard
  2. Locate One-click exclusions
  3. Click on the drop-down menu and exclude theme/plugin/service from JS delay by ticking the checkbox
  4. Click Save to apply the changes

Note:

If you have issues with any of the plugin/theme/services in the drop down menu of the One-click exclusions, try excluding them from JS delay.

If a specific JavaScript file is causing problems, you can exclude the JavaScript file from delay. 

Fixing website scroll issues

Website scrolling issues could include:

  • Missing scroll

To resolve these issues:

  1. Navigate to Website Booster > Settings in your 10Web dashboard
  2. Go to Fix website scroll issue and click the drop-down menu
  3. Choose each method to determine the one that works
  4. Click Save to apply the changes
  5. If no method works, choose Disabled

If this doesn't fix the issue, reduce the optimization level from 10Web Booster's main page or disable Critical CSS.

Fixing website styling issues

Styling issues can take various forms, such as:

  • Shifts in the layout
  • Misaligned text and images
  • Incorrect colors or gradients
  • Disappearance of custom styles

To correct these issues:

  1. Navigate to Website Booster > Settings in your 10Web dashboard
  2. Find the Critical CSS option and disable it
  3. Click Save to implement the changes

If the issue is not resolved, you can exclude CSS files responsible for your styles.

Important:

Deleting the wp-content/cache/ and admin-bar.min.css will result in the unexpected behavior of your website.

Remember, changes made to the Critical CSS or JavaScript Delay options will affect your current optimization level. Don't forget to Save your changes when you are finished customizing.

articles.name: What Optimization Level Should I Choose in 10Web Booster?
articles.title: What Optimization Level Should I Choose in 10Web Booster?
articles.body:
Choosing the right optimization level for your website using 10Web Booster can be a tricky process as it largely depends on your website's specific needs and the trade-off you are willing to make between performance and stability. 10Web Booster provides four levels of optimization that you can select from.

Note:

After changing modes, your website will be re-optimized according to the new settings. The changes will take effect once the optimization process is complete.

Standard and balanced 

These are the two most reliable yet least aggressive levels. Standard and Balanced modes implement several speed optimization techniques to boost your website's performance without overly changing your site's functioning. They use native browser techniques for loading resources, ensuring safety but might compromise a bit on page speed.

Strong 

The Strong level is faster and more aggressive compared to Standard and Balanced. It incorporates advanced features like automatic image lazy loading and delay of all JavaScript, meaning that all JS will load upon interaction. While the Strong level changes the way resources are loaded, it does not interfere with your website's stability and delivers a good balance between speed and dependability.

Extreme

This is our most aggressive and high-performing level. Extreme mode incorporates all the features of the previous modes, plus prioritizes the loading of critical CSS and JavaScript delay, aiming for the highest possible page speed scores. However, for some JavaScript-heavy websites, Extreme mode might not be the optimal choice. If your website falls into this category, we recommend testing the Extreme mode on a few pages to evaluate its performance.

Remember, choosing the correct optimization level largely depends on your website's individual requirements and your preference for stability versus speed.

Each level in 10Web Booster offers a unique combination of optimization settings for best performance and stability. If you need more control over individual settings, you might want to consider using the Advanced settings of the 10Web Booster. 

Note:

If you have a hosted website on 10Web, you can also apply the Pro Level of optimization. The Pro level of optimization enables the Cloudflare CDN on top of your current level of optimization.

articles.name: Intro to 10Web Booster's Advanced Settings
articles.title: Intro to 10Web Booster's Advanced Settings
articles.body:
At 10Web, we are committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that enhance your website’s performance and user experience. As part of this commitment, we are thrilled to introduce the Advanced Settings feature within the 10Web Booster plugin. This new addition empowers you to take complete control over your website optimization process, providing the flexibility and customization you need to achieve your desired outcomes.

Accessing and understanding advanced settings in 10Web Booster

10Web Booster includes a robust set of advanced optimization settings designed to give you granular control over how your website performs. These options let you fine-tune the balance between loading speed, performance, and visual fidelity, ensuring a smoother user experience without compromising on design. To access Advanced Settings, you need to:

  1. Log in to your 10Web dashboard.
  2. Select the website you want to optimize and click on Manage button.
  3. Find the Booster plugin section and go to Settings.

Breakdown of advanced settings

JavaScript Optimization

  • JavaScript Delay: Postpones the loading of JavaScript files until the user interacts with the page (e.g., scrolls or clicks). This can drastically speed up your site’s initial load.
  • Excluded JavaScript Files: Manually specify scripts you don't want to delay or optimize—ideal for ensuring compatibility with essential functions.
  • One-Click Exclusions: Quickly exclude entire themes, plugins, or third-party services from JavaScript delay to prevent potential conflicts.
  • JavaScript Aggregation: Combines multiple JavaScript files into one to minimize HTTP requests, helping the page load faster.
  • JavaScript Minification: Strips out unnecessary characters like spaces and comments from your scripts to reduce file size without affecting functionality.

CSS Optimization

  • Critical CSS: Extracts and prioritizes only the CSS needed to render above-the-fold content. You can toggle this on or off depending on your theme or layout.

  • CSS Aggregation: Merges multiple CSS files into a single file to reduce server requests and improve load times.
  • Excluded CSS Files: Allows you to exclude specific stylesheets from the Critical CSS generation.
  • Inline CSS Extraction: Places essential CSS directly within HTML elements to improve rendering speed for important styles.

  • CSS Minification: Removes redundant characters (spaces, line breaks, comments) from CSS files, reducing their size and improving performance.

 Font Optimization

  • Font Optimizer: Toggles font optimization on or off, which helps reduce the loading time of custom web fonts.

Fix Website Scroll Issues

If your site encounters scroll-related bugs after optimization, this setting provides tailored solutions via a dropdown menu to restore smooth scrolling behavior.

Lazy Loading

Lazy Load for images defers the loading of images until they're about to appear in the user’s viewport, speeding up the initial page load.

  • Lazy Load for Background Images: Applies the same concept to background images, improving load time without sacrificing design.
  • Iframe Lazy Loading: Delays the loading of embedded content like YouTube videos or Google Maps until users scroll near them.
  • Video Lazy Loading: Postpones the loading of video files to avoid slowing down your page, especially useful for media-heavy sites.

Note:

Lazy loading is a site-wide setting—disabling it will affect your entire website. This can lead to slower loading times, particularly on pages with many images, videos, or embedded content, as all media will load immediately instead of only when needed.

The availability and default state of certain advanced settings may vary depending on the optimization mode you're using (e.g., Standard, Balanced, Extreme). Some options will be toggled on or off automatically to align with the selected mode's performance goals

Which advanced settings are enabled in each level 

Depending on the mode you are using, some of the advanced settings will be ticked on or off.

Optimization level JavaScript Delay Critical CSS Font Optimization Lazy Load
Conservative No No No Yes
Balanced No Yes Yes Yes
Strong Yes No Yes Yes
Extreme Yes Yes Yes Yes

Saving changes

Once you make any adjustments, the Save button will become active. Click it to apply your changes.

If you've updated key settings like Critical CSS or JavaScript Delay, a popup notification will appear to inform you that your optimization level will be adjusted accordingly. This ensures that your custom settings remain aligned with overall site performance goals.

articles.name: How to Flush Your DNS Cache
articles.title: How to Flush Your DNS Cache
articles.body:
What is DNS cache

Caching is the storing of information in a server for a quicker retrieval. Complete DNS lookup requires the passage and exchange of information between multiple machines. DNS cache is the storing of previous DNS lookups on an operating system or a browser. This is done so that retrieval of an IP address is quick and efficient. 

When should DNS cache be flushed

Here are some instances when you may need to flush your DNS cache.

  • The website has been updated but you are seeing an old version
  • DNS has been resolved but your not seeing it on your system
  • You are getting error messages
  • You want to update any changes made to your DNS records

You can flush your DNS cache in the case of all of the above. When you flush the DNS cache, you will trigger a complete DNS lookup. This means that if you have any old data, old server DNS, or corrupted DNS servers, all of that data will be deleted and a clean beginning to end lookup of your DNS will be triggered. 

How to flush DNS cache

DNS cache is flushed using a different code which is dependent on the operating system you are using. In all cases, to flush the DNS cache of an operating system, you will need to access its command prompt or command line. 

Windows

To flush the DNS cache on Windows 7 through 10+ systems:

  1. To open the command prompt click the Window button + R 
  2. Type cmd and click Ok
  3. In the command prompt window, type ipconfig /flushdns then press Enter

A message confirming that the DNS cache has been flushed should appear.

Note:

If you are accessing the command prompt for the first time, you may be asked to confirm by typing Yes then pressing enter. If you are asked for login credentials enter them then right-click on your mouse. If you don’t have the credentials, contact your system administrator.

Mac OS

The code to flush the DNS cache of a Mac OS will differ depending on the version of the operating system. 

To flush the cache of a Mac OS:

  1. Click on Finder > Applications > Utilities > Terminal or
  2. Search for Terminal in the Launchpad
  3. Type in the code according to your version:
     

    MacOS Version

    Command
    12 Monterey sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    11 Big Sur sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.15 Catalina sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.14 Mojave sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.13 High Sierra sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.12 Sierra sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.11 El Capitan sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.10 Yosemite sudo discoveryutil udnsflushcaches
    10.9 Mavericks sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.8 Mountain Lion sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.7 Lion sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
    10.6 Snow Leopard sudo dscacheutil -flushcache
    10.5 Leopard sudo lookupd -flushcache
    10.4 Tiger lookupd -flushcache
  4. After entering the code, you’ll be prompted to enter your computer password if you have one and click enter

Please be aware that while typing the password into your terminal, the password will not be visible to you but it is there.

Note:

If you don’t have a password, please contact your system administrator.

Chrome

Note:

If you are using Chrome as your default browser, you will need to flush the DNS cache of Chrome along with your operating system DNS.

To flush the DNS cache of Chrome:

  1. Copy and paste the following URL into your browser: chrome://net-internals/#dns
  2. Click Clear host cache

articles.name: Intro to 10Web Booster
articles.title: Intro to 10Web Booster
articles.body:
10Web Website Booster is designed to automatically optimize your websites front and backends, optimizing the frontend speed and hosting, or, backend performance. 

Frontend optimization 

High PageSpeed scores lead to better SEO ranking, user experience, and increase your customer retention. With precise attention aimed at optimizing your websites using the standards set by PageSpeed Insights, we have built the framework for the best automated optimization possible for websites of any complexity. 

With the 10Web Website booster, your websites will: 

  • Receive a 90+ PageSpeed score
  • Pass Core Web Vitals
  • Get optimized backend

Core Web Vitals was developed by Google to measure how your pages perform. CWV are a set of metrics Google considers and defines as important in the overall user experience of a webpage.  Together with PageSpeed Insights, these make up the ultimate best practices for SEO and ranking your websites. The main focus of core web vitals is measuring user experience using these three aspects: how fast your pages load, interactivity, and visual stability.

We have automated the entire process by having the plugin analyze and detect the type of optimization that will best optimize WordPress websites of any complexity. 

Note:

The free version of 10Web Booster optimizes only the frontend of your websites with a limited number of pages. To have unlimited optimization of the frontend and backend of your websites, upgrade to our Pro plans. 

Here are the techniques we use to optimize your websites and speed up your sites to a 90+ PageSpeed score, increase your ranking, engagement, and conversions.

  • CSS Optimization: Minification of the CSS code removes unnecessary data such as white space, comments, and detailed names, consolidating your codes. The 10Web Booster uses these techniques to render a lighter code which will take less time to fetch and will load faster, making sure that your users have a better experience while using your websites.
  • HTML Optimization: The 10Web Booster uses the technique of minification and compression of HTML to optimize your website code. While minification removes white spaces, comments and detailed names, compression removes repeating information and replaces long words with abbreviations or numbers. File compression is usually done using a lossless compression algorithm. This means that the files will not lose any of their data and are fully recoverable after decompression. However, media files such as image, audio, and video files may be compressed using lossy compression, meaning some loss in quality.
  • JS Minification: Remove unnecessary data such as white spaces, making the code size smaller. 
  • Page Cache Frontend: Caching a page saves the page on a server. 10Web cache is enabled on non-hosted websites only, to make sure that your static HTML pages are saved. This way, in case your users go to access your website again, they will have a faster return because PHP will not need to generate an HTML page, instead the saved HTML will be returned. 
  • Defer JS and CSS Execution: this technique postpones the execution of CSS and Javascript code until the page has been parsed, improving page speed and performance. 
  • Image Optimization: Automatic optimization of images for up to 40% without compromising their quality. 
  • Critical CSS Generation: CSS or cascading style sheet is the code that determines the layout and look of your website. Critical CSS is everything the user will see above the fold for the particular size and resolution of their screen. By generating critical CSS for your site, you have the opportunity to quickly display the requested landing page while the rest of your site loads in the background. 
  • Image, iFrame, and Video Lazy load: Lazy load postpones the loading of non essential images until the user interacts. For example, after the images of the landing page have loaded and the user needs to scroll down to view the rest of the page, this is when the rest of the page will load, upon interaction. In the same way, if the user clicks to open the blog page where there are iFrames and Videos, this is when those will load. In short, loading priority is given to the page and parts of the website you will first see on your screen. By using the lazy loading technique, processing resources are saved and used only as needed; thus, greatly reducing the load time of your website. 
  • Font Swap: Opens page with a generic font while your custom fonts load allowing the user quick access to your website. 
  • Conversion of Image Format to WebP: WebP image format was created by Google and provides a smaller file size for the same image quality. To further optimize your websites, we convert images to webP and serve webP where possible. This enables your websites to load faster. If the browser doesn’t support WebP, then the original images will be served. 
  • Container Specific Image Resizing: Automatically resizes the images to fit the containers used to build your website. Your users will not see a website that has images blocking, on top of each other, or out of their specified containers. Thus, increasing the quality of user experience.  

Hosting performance

Note:

Hosting optimization is available in Pro plans only. To optimize the backend of your website, please take a look at this article.

To get websites that are working seamlessly, fast, and provide the best user experience, you need to have a hosting provider that can accommodate you with the proper environment and support. Your hosting solution is key to how your backend will function. 

Here are performance benchmarks that should be met if your website's backend is optimized:

  • Server performance benchmark: Measures the performance of MySQL and PHP by by running tests that measure the speed of 10,000 mathematical functions, 10,000 string manipulation functions, 10,000 increments, and 10,000 conditional checks in PHP. The server tests 1,000,000 ENCODE(s) with a random string. All of the above is done in 10 seconds or less. 10Web guarantees the optimal time for best performance, which is 10 seconds or less.
  • WordPress benchmark: Measures the speed at which 1000 queries & 250 inserts, select, update and delete functions through $wpdb are done. The best time for good performance is achieved within 8 seconds or less. With 10Web hosting, this score is guaranteed as a part of backend optimization.
  • PHP version: PHP version impacts the speed and performance of your websites. For optimal results, PHP version should be 7.4 or above. 10Web supports the latest versions of the PHP which are lighter and faster. 

If your website is hosted elsewhere, in the Hosting Performance section under Website Booster, you will find a comparison of your site with your current hosting and if it was hosted at 10Web.

10Web hosting uses next generation hosting infrastructure, the best Google cloud servers and SSDs, Nginx, FastCGI caching, and the latest versions of PHP and MySQL. On top of this, 10Web hosting is powered by the Google Cloud platform ensuring a secure and fast delivery of your sites with a guaranteed 99% uptime.

Note:

For 10Web-hosted websites, the Hosting Performance section is located under Hosting Services.

What is Cloudflare

Cloudflare is essentially a website security infrastructure that provides DNS and CDN with added tools and features that make your connections secure, fast and private, offering DDos protection, firewalls, proxies, reverse proxies, SSL & TLS, API, and much more.  

How to point your domain to 10Web when using Cloudflare 

If you would like to use Cloudflare services with 10Web hosting, management of your DNS records should be in Cloudflare and you can point your domain to 10Web using an A record. 

To point your domain: 

  1. Log in to your 10Web account
  2. Click on the website where you want to point your domain
  3. Click on Domains
  4. Click on Add Domain

    Note:

    Please make sure that your domain has not been added elsewhere. In the case that it has, please make sure that you remove it before adding and pointing to 10Web.

  5. Fill In your domain name and click Add Domain
  6. To the left of the dashboard, click on Credentials
  7. Find and copy your IPv4 address 
  8. Log in to your Cloudflare dashboard
  9. Go to DNS management
  10. Leave the hostname empty or enter an @
  11. Add the A record by pasting your IPv4 address in the value field.

Note:

It may take up to 24 hours for the new records to resolve and changes to take effect.

You can use a third party tool to check if your address has been resolved.

Once your address has been resolved, you will need to make the domain primary. 

To make your domain primary:

  1. Click on Domains
  2. Find the domain you have pointed
  3. Click Make Primary

    Note:

    Click the tick off and make sure the 10Web free SSL is not enabled.

  4. Click Confirm

Using 10Web free SSL with Cloudflare

All websites hosted on 10Web are provided with a free SSL certificate from Let’s Encrypt. 

Important:

A redirection loop will occur if you have enabled the 10Web free SSL certificate and your Cloudflare encryption mode is set to flexible.

To generate a free SSL certificate with 10Web for a proxied domain:

  1. Go to your Cloudflare dashboard 
  2. To the left of the dashboard, click on DNS
  3. Go to your domain click Edit 
  4. Under Proxy status click the toggle to DNS only

    Important:

    If you have both yourdomain.com & www.yourdomain.com, please make sure to change the proxy status of both to DNS only.

  5. Click Save 
  6. Log in to your 10Web account
  7. Click on the website where you want to generate the SSL certificate
  8. Click on Tools located to the left of the dashboard
  9. Generate a free SSL certificate
  10. Next go to your Cloudflare dashboard
  11. Go to DNS 
  12. Navigate to your domain and click edit
  13. Under Proxy status for your domain, turn the toggle to Proxied
  14. Click Save
  15. To the left of the dashboard, click on SSL/TLS
  16. Set the encryption to Full

Using Cloudflare SSL while hosting on 10Web 

When Cloudflare proxy is turned on, you are automatically using the SSL provided by Cloudflare. In this case, you can choose to have your proxy encryption mode set to Flexible or Full. 

To turn the proxy on in Cloudflare:

  1. Go to your Cloudflare dashboard
  2. Go to DNS 
  3. Navigate to your domain and click edit
  4. Under Proxy status for your domain, turn the toggle to Proxied
  5. Click Save
  6. To the left of the dashboard, click on SSL/TLS
  7. Set the encryption to Flexible or Full.

Important:

You should not generate the free SSL certificate offered by 10Web with your Cloudflare proxy set to Flexible. Doing this will create a redirection loop.

articles.name: Intro to 10Web DNS
articles.title: Intro to 10Web DNS
articles.body:
What is DNS? 

The Domain Name System is a system for matching the domain name to the IP addresses (Internet Protocol) it is identified with, much like the name in your phonebook that matches the phone number of the person it belongs to. Because it is easier for humans to remember words, the domain name is entered into the browser by the user, and computers match it to the IP address it belongs to, and return the requested domain to the user by, for example, launching the website.

How DNS works

There are four DNS servers working together to fulfill client requests. 

  • DNS resolver: Designed to receive the request and then make an additional request to the root nameserver. Information about root nameservers is consolidated into the DNS resolver. Some resolvers use cache, allowing for faster delivery of requests. 
  • Root nameserver: Translates the root domain, otherwise human language, to the IP address that it belongs to and determines which Top Level Domain it uses. 
  • TLD nameserver: Determines the DNS server the domain is hosted on. Sends a request to the DNS server, for example Amazon route 53. 
  • Authoritative nameserver: Confirms the domain and the IP address match, sends the IP address back to the browser, and the requested web page is then opened in the browser. 

10Web Premium DNS

Unlike most hosting providers, 10Web provides Premium DNS. Premium DNS providers are better equipped to quickly handle a large scale attack, offering a high level of security at all times. They are also more reliable and allow for more control and configuration of your DNS. One of the most important aspects of premium DNS is speed and redundancy. When using multiple servers spread out across the globe, requests to your website are answered faster, as the server that is closest to the query is the one used to answer. 

We use Amazon Route 53 for all domains hosted on 10Web. The AWS Route 53 DNS infrastructure is secure, fast, scalable, and is one of the most powerful DNS services available. 

Once you host a domain on 10Web, a zone is created in AWS Route 53 with the 4 nameservers that you get in your dashboard. After pointing your domain with nameservers, you can start managing your premium DNS through the 10Web dashboard. 

Next step

Manage your DNS records from the 10Web dashboard

The Activity Log feature in 10Web allows workspace owners to track and manage all user activities within their workspace. This feature offers detailed information about user actions, providing insight into who performed specific tasks and when they were completed.

How to use the Activity Log feature

To use the Activity Log feature:

  1. Log into your 10Web account
  2. Click on your workspace drop down menu
  3. Under User & Team Management, click on Activity Log. You can directly access the 10Web Dashboard activity log page where you can view user activity in all of your workspaces using this link: https://my.10web.io/activity-log.

Note:

Only workspace owners have access to the activity log.

The Activity log page consists of filters, located at the top of the page, a Reset button for the filters, and a list of all the activities of your workspace. You can filter the activities you want to view, by Users, Actions, and the Date. 

Note:

If that website has the staging environment enabled, you will activate a 5th filter where you can choose to see actions for the live or staging sites. 

The activity list has the following information:

  • User: The person who has done the action.
  • Type: At what part of the platform was the action done (e.g. hosting, workspace, account, etc.).
  • Action: What was done (e.g. enabling staging environment, changing email, installing plugin, etc.).  
  • Date: When the action was performed.
  • Status: A green checkmark is a successfully completed action and an x for a failed action. 

Note:

If a user is removed, their actions will remain in the activity log.

articles.name: How to Point a Subdomain to 10Web
articles.title: How to Point a Subdomain to 10Web
articles.body:
What is domain

A domain is a human-friendly name given to a main website associated with a unique IP address used by computer systems to call a website.

Example of a domain: yourdomain.com

What is subdomain

Subdomains are subsites within your main or root domain. Subdomains are used for blogs, e-commerce websites, creating your site in different languages, etc. 

Example of a subdomain: blog.yourdomain.com

Note:

When creating or migrating websites to 10Web, you can choose to point a subdomain to a separate WP install. Subdomains are highly customizable and can be used as separate sites that have separate WordPress installations. They can have separate DNS records from the main domain but cannot have separate nameservers from the main domain.

There are two cases when pointing subdomains to 10Web. 

  1. Your main website is hosted at 10Web pointed with either an A record or Nameservers.
  2. When your main website is hosted elsewhere.

Pointing subdomain when main domain is hosted on 10Web

Before you start the process of pointing a subdomain to your main domain, please make sure your main domain is pointed properly.

 

Websites that have their main domain hosted on 10Web can have the main domain pointed using an A record or using nameservers. If your main domain is pointed to 10Web using nameservers, your DNS management will be in 10Web. If you have pointed your main domain using an A record, your DNS management will be where your nameservers are pointed. 

Main domain pointed to 10Web with nameservers

You may want to create and host your subdomain elsewhere or create and host it on 10Web. In either case, here is how you can point your subdomain. 

Pointing subdomain to a website hosted on 10Web

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click Manage on the site where you want to point a subdomain
  3. Under Hosting Services, click on Domains
  4. Click Add Domain
  5. Fill in the name of your subdomain (eg. example.yourdomain.com)
  6. Click Add Domain

  7. Once your address has resolved, click on Make Primary then Confirm

Note:

A CNAME and an A record will automatically be created for your subdomain.

 

Pointing a subdomain to a website hosted elsewhere

To point a subdomain to a website hosted elsewhere, you will need to know the IPv4 address of your hosting provider.

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard

  2. Click on the website of your main domain

  3. Under hosting services, click on Domains

  4. Click on Manage DNS of the main domain

  5. Go to your hosting provider and copy the IPv4 address provided by your hosting company 

  6. Go back to the 10Web dashboard & click on Add a DNS record

  7. From the drop down menu under Type, choose to add an A record

  8. For Hostname add the Sub of your main domain (eg. blog.)

  9. Add the IPv4 address in the corresponding field

  10. Click Add DNS Record

Redirecting subdomains to main domain

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click on the website where you want your subdomain to redirect
  3. Under hosting services, click on Domains
  4. Click on Add Domain
  5. Enter your subdomain and click Add Domain

Main domain pointed to 10Web with an A record

Pointing a subdomain to a website hosted on 10Web

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click on the website where you want to point a subdomain
  3. Under hosting services, click on Domains
  4. Click on Add Domain
  5. Enter your subdomain and click Add Domain
  6. Navigate to Credentials
  7. Copy the IPv4 address
  8. Go to the manage DNS settings of your hosting provider (where your nameservers are pointed)
  9. Under DNS records, add an A record with your newly created subdomain using the 10Web IPv4 address. 
  10. Click Save
  11. In your 10Web dashboard, navigate to Domains
  12. Once your address resolves, find your subdomain and click Make Primary

Important:

If you want to point your subdomain to a website hosted elsewhere, you will need to point it with an A record to where your nameservers are pointed. 

Note:

If you would like to redirect your www.yourdomain.com to yourdomain.com, you will need to also set up a CNAME record with your domain registrar.

Important:

Adding DNS records will vary depending on your domain registrar.

Pointing a subdomain to 10Web when the main website is hosted elsewhere

  1. Log into your 10Web dashboard
  2. Click on the website to which you want to point the subdomain
  3. Under hosting services, click on Domains
  4. Click on Add Domain
  5. Enter your subdomain and click Add Domain
  6. Navigate to Credentials
  7. Copy the IPv4 address
  8. Go to the manage DNS settings of your hosting provider (where your nameservers are pointed)
  9. Under DNS records, add an A record with your newly created subdomain using the 10Web IPv4 address. 
  10. Click Save
  11. In your 10Web dashboard, navigate to Domains
  12. Once your address has resolved, find your subdomain and click Make Primary

articles.title: Workspace and User Roles
articles.body:
Workspaces

The user and team management tool contains two types of workspaces for collaboration and productivity: 

  • Own workspace: You are the owner of this workspace and you can invite users and give them specific roles with varying permission levels.
  • Other workspaces: Workspaces to which you are invited and where you have a specific role and permission level. 

Quick tip:

You can test our user and team management feature for free!

GET STARTED FOR FREE

Important:

Granting permissions to users allows you to safely manage and collaborate. As an added measure of security and for keeping your data safe, It is important that the same login credentials are not used by several individuals at the same time.

Own workspace

The Own workspace belongs only to the account holder and cannot be transferred. As the owner of the workspace, you have permission to everything concerning the account. You are the sole responsible for:

  • Account settings: Personal information, login and security information, and the management of workspaces to which you have access. 
  • User & team management: The management of users of your workspace. 
  • Website migration: Only the owner of a workspace has the permission to migrate a website to their 10Web account.    

Besides the three above mentioned, administrative and developer permissions of your workspace can be granted to other users. 

User roles

To collaborate with your team, you will need to invite them to your own workspace. There are 3 levels of permission or roles in the 10Web user and team management feature.

Admin

Admins have complete access to the workspace including access to adding and removing websites, website DNS, subscription plans, billing details, payment methods, invoices, and all administrative aspects of the workspace except user management and website migration.  

Note:

Access to multisite will allow access to all of the subsites in the multisite network.

Contributor

Access to adding, removing, and managing all websites in the workspace. No access to user management, white label, billing, and website migration. Perfect for lead developers & project managers. 

Member

Access only to a selected websites' live or staging environment. Perfect for clients, developers, designers or marketers.

Switching between workspaces

Workspaces to which you have permissions and your own workspace are located to the left of your dashboard with your own workspace at the top. Each workspace has its own tile. 

Note:

Hovering on individual tiles will show you the complete title of the workspace and your role in it.

To switch between workspaces:

  1. In the left column, find the workspace you want to switch to 
  2. Click on the corresponding tile 

Note:

User and team management is available for all hosting plans and AppSumo plans. At this time, it is not available for plugin plans, bundle plans, and trial plans. Trial plan users can try this feature at no cost for 7 days by upgrading to a paid plan. You can cancel at any time during the 7-day trial and your card will not be charged.

articles.body:
Manage your workspace users and permissions effortlessly with the User & Team Management section in your 10Web dashboard. Invite, edit roles, or remove users quickly while maintaining control over access and security.

User & team management

Invite, remove, or change the permissions of your own workspace users from the User & Team management section of your workspace dashboard.

To manage:

  1. Log into your 10Web account
  2. Click on the drop-down menu of your workspace
  3. Click on Users You can directly access the User and team management page in the 10Web dashboard where you can invite users to your workspace, delete users, change user status, and resend invitations using this link: https://my.10web.io/user-management.

Adding new users

You can invite users by clicking on the Invite or Invite Users button from the top bar of your dashboard, from the dropdown menu of your workspace, or from the User and Team management page.

After clicking the button:

  1. Fill in the complete email addresses of the users you want to invite

    Note:

    You can invite up to 10 users at once separated with commas.

  2. Next, choose the role type from the dropdown menu
  3. Click Invite Users. 

If you have chosen to invite someone with the role of a Member

  1. Click the Select Sites dropdown menu
  2. Select the site you want the member to access
  3. If a website has a staging environment enabled, select Full access or 
  4. Select Staging only to give access to the staging environment only 

The invited users will be added to the list of your users in the User & Team Management section of your workspace with a pending status next to their name. Once the invitation has been accepted, the pending tag will disappear. If the user has a 10Web account, the user will be prompted to login. If the user doesn’t have an account, they will be prompted to create a free account with 10Web. 

Note:

Invitations will stay active for 7 days only. In case you have sent the invitation to the wrong email address, by removing the invitation, you will disable the invitation link to your workspace.

Managing users

In the User & Team Management  section of your workspace, you will see a list of users you have invited to your workspace. Displayed on the list are information about each user. 

Find their:

  • Name 
  • Email
  • Role
  • Sites

In this section, you can also resend an invitation, edit the user’s role, and remove a user. 

If you would like to invite the user again, click on the Resend button at the right of each user.

Removing a user

To remove a user from your workspace:

  1. Click on the three dots at the right of the user
  2. Click Remove user
  3. Enter your password

    Note:

    Here is how to reset your password if  you have forgotten it. 

  4. Click Yes, Remove

Note:

Removed users will be notified by email about their removal from your workspace.

Deleting users from the WP dashboard

For security purposes and for tracking the actions in your own workspace, the first time a new user logs in and accesses a website of your workspace, a user is created in the WP admin of that website with their email address. 

When the user is deleted from the workspace in your 10Web dashboard, the user still exists in the WP dashboard. You will need to manually find this user, and delete them from the WP dashboard. 

To delete a user from your 10Web workspace and from the WP dashboard of the website:

  1. Click on the workspace dropdown menu of your 10Web dashboard
  2. Delete the user from your workspace
  3. Click on the website the user had access to
  4. Click on the icon to go to the WP admin dashboard
  5. To the left of the dashboard, click on Users
  6. Find the user from the list click on the red Delete located under the user email
  7. Choose to delete all content or choose to attribute all the content to a user
  8. Click Confirm Deletion 

Editing a user role

To change the role of a user:

  1. Click on the edit icon located at the right of each user
  2. Click on the dropdown menu and choose the new role
  3. Click Update

articles.name: Cannot Reset My Password. What Should I Do?
articles.title: Cannot Reset My Password. What Should I Do?
articles.body:
If you've forgotten your 10Web account password or never set one up (for example, if you signed up with Google), don't worry. You can easily reset your password from the login screen or via your 10Web dashboard. This article provides detailed instructions on how to troubleshoot issues if you're not receiving the password reset email.

If you did not receive the password reset email

Please, follow the instructions below in case you did not receive the password reset email:

Step 1: Check the email associated with your 10Web account

Ensure you're checking the correct email inbox. Password reset emails and other account-related notifications are sent to the email address linked to your 10Web account. If you're unsure which email you used, check if you have ever gotten any emails from 10Web under that account. If none are found, you may need to check other email addresses.

If you have access to your 10Web Dashboard, you can find your account email address here.

Step 2: Check your spam or junk folders

Sometimes password reset emails might be incorrectly marked as spam by your email provider. Look in your spam or junk folder. If you find the email there, move it to your inbox and mark it as important to ensure future messages from 10Web are delivered correctly.

Step 3: Reset your password again

If you've checked the correct email and your spam folder but still haven't received the password reset email, attempt to reset your password again.

Step 4: Contact customer support

If all else fails and you’re still not receiving the reset email, reach out to 10Web’s customer support for assistance using live chat available 24/7. 

If you do not have access to the email associated with your 10Web account

To reset your 10Web password, you need access to the email linked to your account. If you’ve lost access to this email, try recovering it through your email service provider. 

If recovery isn’t possible, contact 10Web customer support with an account recovery request.

Boost your revenue with 10Web’s AI-Powered WordPress platform by earning up to 30% commission for referrals, one of the top affiliate commission rates in the industry.

How does the affiliate program work?

We collaborate with you to provide promotional materials, such as logos, visuals, and video product demonstrations, which allow you to demonstrate to your audience the capabilities of 10Web's AI-Powered WordPress platform. This platform boosts website speed and uses the latest AI technologies to accelerate website and content creation.

By referring your audience to 10Web, you provide value and build trust since you are directing them to a genuinely helpful product featuring top-tier technology and expert customer support.

How to join the 10Web Affiliate Program

The 10Web Affiliate Program runs on Impact, a reliable partner platform that tracks affiliate performance, manages commissions, and facilitates payments. This guide walks you through how to register, manage your affiliate dashboard, and ensure your earnings are correctly processed.

To sign up for the 10Web Affiliate Program through Impact, follow these steps:

  1. Go to the 10Web Affiliates Page.
  2. Click Become an affiliate.
  3. Accept the affiliate agreement terms in the pop-up.
  4. Select a registration method: email, Google, LinkedIn, etc.
  5. Enter your personal details, including mobile number.
  6. Choose your business category based on how you interact with your audience.
  7. Click Continue and choose all applicable promotion methods.
  8. Add your website URL.
  9. Fill in the “Tell us about yourself” section.
  10. Select your preferred currency and click Submit.

Important:

Have your tax and company information ready and verify your account through email to complete the signup.

Accessing tracking links

Once your application is approved, you can find your affiliate tracking links on your Impact dashboard:

  1. Navigate to Create a Link.
  2. To change the landing page, enter a new URL in the destination field and click Create.

     

Accessing banner ads

You can add visual content to your website using banners:

  1. Go to Content > Assets> Images tab in your Impact dashboard.

  2. Select the ad you want, then click Get Ad Code or Get Tracking Link.
  3. Copy and embed the HTML code into your site.

Setting up payment preferences

To receive commissions, configure your payout settings:

  1. In your Impact dashboard, go to Balance > Bank Account Settings

  2. Select your payment method:
    • PayPal: Enter your PayPal email.
    • EFT: Enter your bank details.

Submitting tax documents

Depending on your location, you must submit a tax form:

  1. Click on your profile icon in the top-right corner.
  2. Select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  3. In the Settings menu, click on Tax Documents.

     
  4. Click Submit Tax Document.
  5. Click Continue to proceed to DocuSign and complete the submission.

Commission payout terms

To ensure transparency and fairness, the following rules govern how and when affiliate commissions are earned and paid.

1. Payout eligibility

  • Commission basis: Commissions are paid based on actual payments received by 10Web from customers referred through your affiliate link.

  • Referral qualification: A referred customer must be entirely new to 10Web. If their Customer ID has existed in our system at any point during the 12 months prior to their first recorded action, the referral will not qualify for commission. This applies to both Platform and API plans.

2. Commission duration

  • Platform plans: Affiliates earn a 30% commission on all payments made by the referred customer for up to 12 months after their first payment.

  • API plans: For monthly subscriptions, affiliates earn 30% commission on all payments made during the first 4 months following the initial payment.

For annual subscriptions, affiliates earn a 10% commission on the first annual payment.

3. Refunds and payment reversals

  • If a customer’s payment is refunded, reversed, or reimbursed before the payout freeze date, the associated commission will be canceled and not paid out.

Questions or concerns

If you have any other questions, feel free to reach out to us at affiliates@10web.io for further assistance.

We look forward to partnering with you to bring innovative products and services to your audience!
